Assignment 05 / Sculpting for Design

Abstract Wiring

Two connected forms. Two ways of filling space. A hanging study in contrast and connection.

Wire · Paper · Positive & negative space

Group project with Sudiksha Suresh and Astha Chand

Working as a group, Medha Girish, Sudiksha Suresh, and Astha Chand planned two connected wire forms that would contrast with one another while belonging to one larger composition.

01

Planning a piece together

Because three people were working on the assignment, the group wanted to make two pieces that could attach to one another and interact. Their brainstorming explored hanging structures before developing an hourglass-like arrangement.

The sketches show possible outlines, suspension points, and the relationship between the upper and lower forms. They also introduce the central question of the work: how might paper change the spaces created by a wire framework?

02

Positive and negative

In their submission, the group describes two attached tetrahedral forms. One uses paper to fill positive spaces created by the wiring; the other fills negative spaces. This opposite treatment gives the two halves a shared language while making them visually distinct.

Wire establishes the edges and connections. The butter paper adds translucent surfaces and cut-away shapes, allowing the surrounding space to remain visible through parts of the sculpture. The irregular paper shapes sit within a more angular framework.

03

An hourglass in space

The photographed construction develops the idea into a hanging, abstract hourglass form. Two tapered sections meet around a narrow connection, with the wider ends extending away from the centre.

These three photographs show how the paper and open gaps read from different viewpoints. Looking around the piece changes which surfaces overlap and which parts of the wire framework are exposed.

04

A proposed home for the work

At the time of the submission, the group planned to paint the wires and butter paper and hang the piece in their hostel wing. The photographs document the construction before that proposed finishing stage.

The project brings collaboration and material contrast together: two connected forms are treated differently, then read as parts of a single suspended object.
